title: `TypeError` when requesting `_stcore/metrics` with sqlalchemy engine in session state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Requesting `/_stcore/metrics` will throw a `TypeError` if an instance of [Engine](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/75ab6b370034e69bc798f9a77751afb200e24f1d/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py#L2926) from sqlalchemy is present in session state.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sqlalchemy
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new python project, installing `streamlit 1.38.0` and `sqlalchemy 2.0.34`
2. Create a `main.py` and copy the above example into it
3. run `main.py` with `streamlit`
4. run `curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics` in another terminal

### Expected Behavior

- No errors in the terminal running Streamlit

- Should return something to the effect of the following from the curl command:
```
❯ curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics
# TYPE cache_memory_bytes gauge
# UNIT cache_memory_bytes bytes
# HELP Total memory consumed by a cache.
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 2120
# EOF
```



### Current Behavior

```
TypeError: cannot create weak reference to '_EmptyListener' object
2024-09-09 17:57:11.617 500 GET /_stcore/metrics (::1) 117.88ms
```

curl response:
```
❯ curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics
<html><title>500: Internal Server Error</title><body>500: Internal Server Error</body></html>
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.38.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: macOS 14.6.1
- Browser: n/a


### Additional Information

This is also reproduceable by placing an instance of the class it's complaining about, `_EmptyListener`, into session state. The following will produce the same error when the `_stcore/metrics` endpoint is requested:

```py
from typing import Any

import streamlit as st
import sqlalchemy
from sqlalchemy.event.attr import _EmptyListener, _ClsLevelDispatch
from sqlalchemy.event.base import _HasEventsDispatch


st.session_state.test = _EmptyListener(
    parent=_ClsLevelDispatch(
        parent_dispatch_cls=_HasEventsDispatch[Any], fn=lambda _: _
    ),
    target_cls=object,
)
```

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-9428)

Hi [USER] thanks for submitting this issue. It seems there's two problems:
1) putting your db connection is session_state isn't the best place for that kind of thing to live. I'd take a look at [`st.connection`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/connections/st.connection) instead
2) this has uncovered an issue with how were measuring memory for session_state as part of our metrics

I'll keep this issue open to track (2), but would recommend you trying (1) to see if it can unblock you.

Fixed by #15334 (merged 2026-05-27). The cache/stats sizing path now goes through a `safe_sizeof()` guard (`lib/streamlit/runtime/stats.py`) that catches the `TypeError: cannot create weak reference` raised when sizing SQLAlchemy objects, so the `/_stcore/metrics` endpoint no longer 500s. (As an extra layer, #15472 also made the expensive memory stats off by default.)

Closing as resolved — please reopen if it recurs on a current release.
